RagShortTexts: In 1260 at Ain Jalut, Mamluk horse archers crushed Kitbuqa, definitively halting Mongol.

Variants.Content: Fought on September 3, 1260, at Ain Jalut ('Spring of Goliath') in Galilee, the battle marked the high-water mark of Mongol conquest. Mamluk Sultan Qutuz and General Baibars executed a masterclass in feigned retreat, encircling Kitbuqa's vanguard in a bloody shock cavalry counter-assault that shattered Mongol invincibility.
Ain Jalut saved Cairo, Damascus, and Mecca from annihilation, firmly cementing Mamluk military prestige across the Near East.
